forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Essex police absorbs pay costs through accounting change while fire faces £0.5m shortfall
news_drafts.lead: Essex Police and Fire Service have revised their 2027/28 budgets after six months of experience with actual pay costs and demand. Police moved from a projected £1.4m shortfall to a £0.7m surplus between June and September, but £2.8m of that £2.1m improvement came from a change in how the force calculates minimum revenue provision (MRP), the amount set aside each year to pay off past borrowing. The underlying position shifted because staff pay awards reached 3.5 per cent against a 2.5 per cent assumption, costing £2.0m more than forecast, while new service demands added £3.4m pressure. Fire Service moved from a balanced 2027/28 budget in February to a £0.5m shortfall by September after a 3.8 per cent pay award for operational staff cost £0.7m against a 2.2 per cent forecast. Together, the two services faced £2.7m in unfunded pay costs. Police also identified £3.4m in new demand that cannot be contained within existing budgets, a pressure that will persist through the medium-term outlook.

news_drafts.headline: Essex pension fund achieved 108% funding level in 2025 valuation as risks rise
news_drafts.lead: The Essex Pension Fund finished the 2025 triennial valuation overfunded at 108%, meaning pension liabilities are covered with a surplus. The fund has maintained clean internal audit opinions for eight consecutive years, with both its funding and investments functions and its administration receiving Good Assurance ratings in 2025/26 and no audit recommendations issued. However, the fund faces emerging pressures: a February 2026 funding-at-risk measure stood at 26.3%, slightly above the 25% target, indicating solvency is marginally more exposed than the fund's tolerance threshold allows. As of August, 17 strategic risks remained above their target scores, with the fund conducting a full review of its risk register to align with revised strategic objectives and incorporate emerging risks including local government reorganisation and artificial intelligence.

news_drafts.headline: Essex Pension Fund receives top audit grade for eighth consecutive year
news_drafts.lead: The Essex Pension Fund has received the highest level of internal audit assurance for the eighth year running, with no recommendations made against any of its key functions. The fund's Funding, Investments and Administration functions all achieved "Good Assurance" in their 2025/26 internal audits, the top grade available. The absence of audit recommendations across all three areas over eight consecutive years indicates sustained strong governance and control within the pension fund's operations. The assurance was reported to the Essex Pension Fund Advisory Board at its meeting on 13 July 2026.

findings.paper_title: Essex Housing Development LLP Trading Update Q1 2026/27
findings.headline: No dividend will be paid to ECC from Essex Housing LLP in 2026/27
findings.detail: Based on the forecast net loss, no dividend distribution is expected in 2026/27 and no distribution has been included in the Council's Medium Term Revenue Strategy.
findings.matters: Finance directors track dividend expectations as revenue sources; zero dividend signals that the LLP is not yet generating surpluses to distribute to the shareholder.
findings.figures: Net loss £383,000; zero dividend expected for 2026/27
findings.quote: Based on the forecast outturn, no dividend is expected to be paid to ECC for 2026/27 and no distribution included in the MTRS.

findings.paper_title: Essex Housing Development LLP Trading Update Q1 2026/27
findings.headline: ECC receives £4.6m in wider benefits from Essex Housing despite the operating loss
findings.detail: Despite the net loss of £383k, ECC receives £1.035m margin on lending, £2.2m in land value payments, £800k overhead cost recovery, and £598k specialist units revenue benefits, totalling £4.6m in wider benefits for 2026/27.
findings.matters: The operating loss needs to be evaluated in context of total value generation; the full economic model shows returns to the council alongside the operational loss.
findings.figures: Margin on Lending £1,035k; Land Values Realised £2,200k; ECC Overhead Cost Benefit £800k; Revenue Benefits from Specialist Units £598k; Total wider benefits £4,600k
findings.quote: ECC continues to realise significant wider financial benefits from Essex Housing LLP.  Excluding the net loss from the LLP, in 2026/27 these benefits are estimated at £4.6m.

findings.paper_title: Essex Housing Development LLP Trading Update Q1 2026/27
findings.headline: Hargrave House paused and Scrub Lane undertaking viability assessment due to market conditions
findings.detail: Hargrave House has paused work to reconsider scheme viability, including considering non-net-zero delivery and removal of planned community facility, citing market conditions. Scrub Lane is undertaking drainage cost assessment which will inform an updated viability assessment. Both delays affect the development pipeline beyond the single 2026/27 sales scheme.
findings.matters: Pipeline scheme delays extend development timelines and increase debt servicing burden; this explains why there is no committed development revenue beyond Essex County Hospital and reduces near-term sales visibility.
findings.figures: Hargrave House 10 homes; Scrub Lane 47 homes
findings.quote: Work was paused to consider options to improve viability on the scheme, including delivering the scheme on a non‑net zero basis and considering the re-provision of community use where the previous proposal has become unviable due to market conditions.

findings.paper_title: Essex Housing Development LLP Trading Update Q1 2026/27
findings.headline: All forecast 2026/27 sales (32 units, £12.669m turnover) depend exclusively on Essex County Hospital scheme
findings.detail: The entire revenue and profit forecast for the year depends on one development scheme. No other committed schemes are forecast to deliver sales in 2026/27. If Essex County Hospital sales underperform or slip, the entire forecast and loss position deteriorates significantly.
findings.matters: Finance directors and lenders assess pipeline diversification and revenue concentration risk; single-scheme dependency creates vulnerability to one project's delivery.
findings.figures: 32 units from Essex County Hospital; £12.669m turnover from one scheme only
findings.quote: Sales during the year relate solely to the the Essex County Hospital scheme, with 32 units forecast to be sold.

findings.paper_title: Essex Housing Development LLP Trading Update Q1 2026/27
findings.headline: Interest payable of £2.296m is the primary driver of the swing from £3.571m gross profit to net loss
findings.detail: Operating overheads of £1.658m plus interest costs of £2.296m combine to convert the gross profit into a loss. The interest burden alone nearly equals the entire gross profit.
findings.matters: High debt servicing costs constrain returns to the council; lenders need to assess whether debt levels are sized appropriately relative to revenue generation.
findings.quote: The movement from gross profit to net loss is primarily driven by operating costs including overheads of £1.658m and £2.296m of interest payable on borrowing.
